## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a Resident / Public reader, shown with
four stat tiles and two dashboard panels (01: Hull map of how strongly the model's predictions
depend on knowing each area's location, the example area outlined; 02: the example area's most
influential features). The example area is public_overview.example_area, chosen as a typical
place, not an extreme one. This section replaces section 14 "Length and form" and its bolding
rule. Every other section, including prohibited claims and the self-check, still applies.

Plain language only: no coefficients, test statistics, GeoSensitivity, LISA or other model
terms. Shares and "out of" counts are fine. Answer what the model pays attention to, never why
crime happens, and never describe residents or communities as risky.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters); label is at most 10 everyday words that make the figure
  meaningful on its own. A count is written as a fraction of its whole. Use exactly these
  four, in this order, each from the named field: public_overview.tile_figures.crime_history_share,
  .built_environment_share, .areas_led_by_six_month_average, and .least_influential_feature
  (its share, naming that same feature).
- "section_01": at most 65 words, across Hull (panel 01): what the model mostly pays attention
  to, what matters comparatively little, and the places (by locality) where predictions depend
  most on knowing where the area is. Do not cite any tile value.
- "section_02": at most 65 words, the example area (panel 02) by locality and its main streets:
  its most influential features and whether its pattern is like Hull's or different. Do not
  cite any tile value or panel figure.
- "footer": one non-causal limitation, at most 15 words.

No repetition: every figure appears ONCE on the card. The panels already print the example
area's rank and its feature shares (public_overview.shown_on_panels), so neither tiles nor
sections cite them; say "panel 02 shows" instead. A tile figure is not cited again in the
sections. Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry
no markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON, and write your own sentences.

illustrative_narrative.section_01: Across Hull the model pays most attention to [[t:recent crime levels]]. Census characteristics such as unemployment come next ([[n:20%]]), then streets, shops and green space. [[t:Road and junction density]] matter very little. Predictions depend most on knowing where an area is in [[t:Old Town]], Dairycoates and Sculcoates.
illustrative_narrative.section_02: In [[t:Stoneferry]], around Stoneferry Road, the model also leans on the six-month crime average, then the three-month average and private renting. Its pattern is [[t:much like Hull's]], and its predictions depend on its location about as much as a [[t:typical area]].
illustrative_narrative.footer: Shows what the model pays attention to, not why crime happens.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch random-donor SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA moves its rows to the centroids of random other Hull LSOAs (50 draws, all other inputs kept), and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. Absolute shifts are larger where predicted crime is higher. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (random-donor design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: random_donor
geo_design.definition: Random-donor design: masking an LSOA moves the coordinates of its rows to the centroid of a random other Hull LSOA (K = 50 draws), all other inputs kept; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the XGBoost model on 30 predictors + easting/northing; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

sign_conventions.local_feature_coefficient: Directional. Masks code a retained player as one and the response is the perturbed minus the original prediction, so a positive value means the area's own value of the feature raises its prediction relative to the masking reference and a negative value lowers it.
sign_conventions.global_feature_coefficient: Not directional: fitted to a non-negative distance; rank by magnitude.
sign_conventions.geo_coefficient: Relative contribution to the coalition response; the sign is not a direction of crime.
sign_conventions.feature_branch_model: One XGBoost model on the substantive predictors plus the centroid coordinates; coordinates are kept at their true values and are not Feature players.

limitations: No RAG / no invented local context.
pattern_scale is not established in the computed outputs.
local_p_adjusted is not available in the published LISA table.

content.section_01: Across Hull, the model pays most attention to [[t:recent crime levels]]. Census details like unemployment and age matter next, while [[t:road density]] and similar features matter very little. Predictions depend most on knowing where an area is in [[t:Old Town]], Dairycoates, Sculcoates, and Stepney.
content.section_02: In [[t:Stoneferry]], around Foster Street and Stoneferry Road, panel 02 shows the six-month and three-month crime averages and private renting are most influential. This pattern is [[t:similar to Hull overall]], with the area's location mattering about as much as in a [[t:typical place]].
content.footer: Shows what the model pays attention to, not why crime happens.
